# MAKE_TIMESTAMP with single argument not working correctly

When using MAKE_TIMESTAMP with a single argument (timestamp in microseconds), it fails to convert it properly.

#### MCVE Code Sample

```python
import sqlglot

# This works fine
sqlglot.parse_one("MAKE_TIMESTAMP(1992, 9, 20, 13, 34, 27.123456)", dialect="duckdb")

# This fails
sqlglot.parse_one("MAKE_TIMESTAMP(1667810584123456)", dialect="duckdb")
```

#### Problem Description

The DuckDB dialect in sqlglot should support both forms of MAKE_TIMESTAMP:
1. MAKE_TIMESTAMP(year, month, day, hour, minute, second) - works correctly
2. MAKE_TIMESTAMP(microseconds) - fails because the code that handles this case was removed

When passing a single argument to MAKE_TIMESTAMP, it should be interpreted as a Unix timestamp in microseconds and converted to a timestamp, but this functionality is broken.

#### Expected Output
The parser should correctly handle both forms of the MAKE_TIMESTAMP function.

#### Reproduction
You can also see this by trying to transpile a query with the single-argument form:

```python
sqlglot.transpile("SELECT MAKE_TIMESTAMP(1667810584123456) AS t", read="duckdb", write="duckdb")
```

This fails because the code no longer handles the single-argument case.
</issue>
